newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee budget calls for 1,800 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee budget calls for 1,800 job cuts.

text.p: Tennessee Gov. Don Sundquist has proposed a $14.4 billion budget for fiscal 1998 that includes no new taxes and cuts nearly 1,800 jobs.
Sundquist's plan, outlined in his state-of-the-state speech Monday night, would lay off 738 workers and eliminate more than 1,000 unfilled positions."
Hardest hit were the Corrections Department and the Department of Health and Mental Retardation, which would lose about 250 jobs each.
Sundquist had previously warned that the state would have to cut more "nonessential" jobs in order to balance the budget. The state projects a $70 million deficit for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30.

"In many respects this is the toughest budget our state has faced in the last five years and the toughest we are likely to face in the next five," Sundquist said. "Balancing the budget in a time of tight revenues requires some choices."
Sundquist's plan called for $135.8 million of bond issues.
It included nearly $500 million of new spending, nearly all for programs that affect children, including education, health and welfare.

To help pay for those increases, Sundquist proposed using $88 million of reserves from the Tennessee Housing Development Agency. He said that could be done without endangering the state's guaranteed loan program.
Sundquist's plan also cuts nearly $40 million from state college and university budgets.
